In addition, the two decades of accelerator use (spanning more than 73,000 combined LIA shots) were enabled by continuous machine monitoring, careful operations, maintenance, and addressing of design issues as they were identified. Continuous advancements through this process are essential to DARHT’s continuing reliability. To extend DARHT’s exquisite experimental data return track record, a diverse suite of projects is needed to address facility aging, equipment failures, code compliance, utility disruptions, LIA improvements, diagnostics advance- ments, and hydrodynamic data management. Appendix I summarizes the near-term (2–5 years), mid-term (5–10 years), and long-term (10–20 years) actions that will enable the three DCX priorities. This strategy covers a very broad set of capabilities, vulnerabilities, improvements, and technical subject areas with concordant advancements or methods of revitalization that are required within the DARHT Complex to enable con- tinued high-quality data return from static and dynamic experiments for national security. In conclusion, the ability to implement the technologies proposed within this strategy depend strongly on mission priorities, maturity of the technology, funding, workforce availability, and laboratory space. Research, development, and/or feasibility studies are required for the proposed technologies to successfully meet the three priorities identified herein. In addition, other ideas and/or concepts may be discovered during these activities that become incorporated under the DCX umbrella. Implementation of the DARHT Capability eXpansion strategy will provide tremendous advancements to extend DARHT’s reliability and resilience, increase the quality and quantity of DARHT data, and enable hydrodynamic measurements in complex environments, ensuring the DARHT Complex remains the nation’s premier hydrodynamic data source for stockpile certification, safety, surety, and emerging global security threats for decades into the future.
